text: I do not live in Tampa, and looked this up via Yelp. If you are alone and on business, you can sit at the bar, and chit chat with them. Second best Sushi "as far as taste and freshness" I have found, other than Syun's in Hillsboro , Oregon. Great find.

text: Oh my. Oh ho ho ho ho my. This is some darn good BBQ. I took the day off last Friday, and I wanted to treat myself to a delicious lunch. I needed to head downtown for some errands, and Bogart's was in the neighborhood. I had been wanting to try it for quite some time, and I figured that would be a good day to try it. I stood in line for about 10 minutes, which gave me time to study the menu and decide what I wanted to get. I heard about the similarities between Pappy's (which I LOVE) and Bogart's, so I knew whatever I ordered was bound to be delicious. I settled with a half rack of ribs, baked beans, and cole slaw. It was a beautiful day, so I sat at one of the tables outside. They had a few tables indoors, but those were all full. Similar to Pappy's, just when I needed a table, one opened up. So outside I went. The food came out pretty quickly, and it all looked delicious. I started with the baked beans. AMAZING. Smoky, a little spicy, and piping hot. I loved these. The cole slaw was equally tasty. It was mayonnaise based, I believe, which gave it a rich creaminess that I adored. SO tasty! On to the main event: the ribs. The meat on these ribs literally fell off the bone, making them extremely easy to eat. I tried a bit of all four sauces Bogart's offered, but I fell in love with their Voodoo Sauce (the spicy one -- of course!). There were a few employees making the rounds to all of the tables to ensure everyone's meals were fine. I gave them the thumbs up, dirty fingers, face, and all. This stuff was GOOD. Unlike Pappy's, Bogart's didn't have a line that wrapped around the block, which was a good thing. However, since I visited on a Friday afternoon, I probably didn't get a true sense of how crowded it could get. In any event, I loved it, and I will DEFINITELY be back! Bogart's and Pappy's in the same city? We St. Louisans sure are lucky!
label: POS

text: Overall my experience at fork was just OK. Granted their menu changes seasonally so maybe this allows everyone to have a different experience. The wild mushroom risotto had perfect flavors. Melted in your mouth. Don't remember what my friends ate, but no one was all that elated with their food. The one thing we still talk about...every day...is the bread pudding. I mean who even cares about bread pudding, but this one changed our minds about what bread pudding should be. It was moist but not mush, which I think was key, but what made it absolutely wonderful was the pairing of flavors. It was chocolate bread and whatever else goes in there and then it had this great mint sauce under it which was divine. Seriously keep looking on their menu and wait for it to come back, you won't regret it. I would have given Fork 3 stars, but just because of the bread pudding I added one more.

text: Two words: PAN ROAST Two more words: order it! I had the combination pan roast...it was incredible! Lots of fresh seafood. Delicious broth that you'll want to sop up with their wonderful bread. I also had the jumbo shrimp cocktail, and it was very good, too. But the pan roast...you have just got to eat this. And, be sure to check out the cool way they cook it. Unique. Excellent service. Our waitress was probably the most attentive without being overly attentive that I have had in years. Prices are very reasonable for the high-quality and excellent tasting food. Only downside is that they will no take reservations. We had a party of 6 so called the day before. The hostess told us to call about an hour before we wanted to eat and they could put us on the list. Not a true reservation, but to get our name on the wait-list. So we called the day we wanted to go, and that hostess would not put us on the list. Not sure what the issue was, but they need to have a consistent policy about this. We were pretty aggravated by the time we got seated over an hour later. We will definitely be back next time we are in Reno. One of the best meals I've had in a long time.

text: The Well seems to have found its stride. And I am so glad. The kitchen is cranking out some delicious comfort foods. My choices during the last three visits were quite satisfying: Smokehouse Burger, Pulled Pork sandwich, Beet salad and Wild Mushrooms which was the best surprise. The beet salad is a big plate of sliced roasted beets, generously sprinkled with goat cheese, a bit of arugula and a perfectly matched vinaigrette. Easily a meal for me. The Wild Mushrooms is actually richly delicious cheesy grits topped with a nice helping of mushrooms and drizzled with truffle oil. It is a luscious appetizer, great in cold weather. I kinda wanna get some now after typing this. They now sell a variety of house-made pickled veggies. Try the pickled mushrooms, the vinegar marinade make them perfect as a salad topper.

Not too tough as we shot pretty well using only 6 clubs (we didn't want to fill up the trunk on our 2000 mile trip). Very nice ... as a golfer who plays about 20 rounds a year, I recommend it.

text: I enjoy beer very much, therefore, I love 1702! Mucho beer on tap + delicious pizza = a VERY happy me! Visited last night for my bf's family get together and it was packed (as usual). We were able to snag a table after waiting for 15 mins. I've only ever had beer at 1702 but was really excited to try the pizza because it always looks so good! To start we ordered the Hop bread and wings. OMG the Hop bread was amazing. It was covered in cheese and garlic and had a hoppy bitter taste that went so well with the warm marinara. The wings were okay. The hot sauce was standard and tasty but the wings were a little soggy....I am not a fan of wiggly chicken skin. I like that were not fried but the skin kinda freaked me out. Aside from wiggly skin the chicken was tender and overall tasty. After we nommed all that, we placed our pizza order: 14" Islanda, hold the Green peppers and a 14" Pepperoni. The Islanda was amazing. I loves LOVES me some cheese and the Islanda was covered is slightly melted Feta...I mean COVERED! mmmm The pepperoni was a standard pepperoni pizza, lots of pepperoni but not too much. The crusts were very crispy on the bottom and soft on top. I can't wait to go back and get their calzone. As far as beer went, my original choice was the Velvet Merlin (Merkin) because after our 10 day long beer and wine tour, the Velvet Merlin was the beer I absolutely fell in love with and it's sold at Total Wine! Just my luck they were all out. The waitress was nice enough to bring a few samples of other similar beers w/o wasting time. I didn't like either so I ordered the Milk stout. That beer is like a meal, very rich and heavy and head is like melted ice cream. I love it. After that I ordered a floral IPA to go along with the pizza. I forget the name but it was good, not something I'd get to casually sip but it did go very well with the Islanda. This be one of my fave places to drink beer!

text: What a wonderful place to visit! Tons of animals to see, modern, open spaces...my kind of place. The place is big, but not so large as to be overwhelming and even though there were many people there, we were still able to enjoy each exhibit and not feel limited because of overcrowding. The single and double strollers were cool, so when the kids got tired we were still able to ride them around comfortably in a double stroller. The staff was spectacular. Everyone was friendly, helpful, willing to give directions, willing to help with your kids... they really consistently went above and beyond. I didn't come across one rude or unprofessional staff member all day. Best exhibits IMO were -- sharks, hippos (my do they stink!!!) and stingrays. We went during the holiday season so we got to see Scuba Santa which is pretty awesome for kids. The one criticism I have is that this place is an absolute money pit. For two kids and two adults, we spent $93 in tickets (got them online the day prior) and then paid for a photo in the sleigh, food, parking, ice cream, face painting, etc. A stuffed animal in the gift shop was $25. No, I'm not joking. So all in all, for the four of us, we spent about $200 for one day. Did we have to do all of this stuff, could we have brought our own food and bypassed the face painting and ice cream... absolutely. But the reality is, the kids wanted to do it and we wanted to have the full experience.. so there.. its partly our fault, lol. The kids had an awesome time and we enjoyed it too but it is truly ridiculously expensive and not something we can afford to do frequently unfortunately. That being said, this place is still awesome and it's worth a visit.
label: POS

The pieces of chocolate were packaged neatly. I love that the truffles are placed in cute Chinese take out boxes. The employee also included a truffles list in my bag, which had each truffle I ordered checked off. This was a nice touch. If you're in need of a chocolate fix, definitely pay a visit to The Cocoa Tree.

I was on a mission to find a few things, and I pretty much knew spending a day here would be a success. For some reason it doesn't seem as big to me anymore, but maybe that's because I've been here so many times that I know it like the back of my hand. Parking wasn't as bad as I thought it would be, we actually scored a spot about 15 meters away from the door, perfect timing I guess. I had to peek into the waterpark and at the sea lions - just for old times sake. I like the waterpark but its way too expensive and I kind of feel sorry for the sea lions. It is pretty cool to think about those things being in a mall though. I didn't get a chance to walk through Galaxyland, which is always fun. They do have a lot of duplicate stores here but I don't mind, and its nice to see some of the old stores are still hanging around. We checked out T&T, crazy busy, but got some good cheap sushi for lunch. Bourbon Street had a bunch of new restaurants that look promising, and of course good ol' Hooters (which evidently, you don't need to have anymore to work there). You can definitely see the malls age now, its starting to look dated, although I LOVE the new fountains/sitting areas as they look very fresh and modern. The mall seems brighter and cleaner as well. A little sad that the big whale is gone, many memories of that, although it did smell really bad and to be honest, it was pretty ugly. Of course I love the new additions, like Anthropologie, Pinkberry, etc. I enjoy coming here on the occasions I'm in Edmonton if I have a whole day to walk around and browse. But I would never come here if I just needed one thing or to get in and out quickly - that would be a nightmare!

text: We went here as a family for my mom-in-laws birthday dinner. The place has a kind of corporate, almost chain-like atmosphere but still very nice. I ordered the Weyerbacher Belgian style triple which was served up properly in a nice goblet. Delicious. For food, we started with a flatbread pizza which was fresh mozzarella, sundried tomato and fresh basil. Crispy flatbread and gooey cheese; the wood fired oven gave it all a nice smoky flavor - very good. For my main course I went with the grilled mahi mahi special which I got blackened - the portion size was kinda small but the fish was delicious. Wife had the seared rare ahi-tuna salad with mixed greens and a delicious soy/ginger dressing. Mom-mom had the scallop special which were perfectly seared large diver scallops, balsamic reduction with sautéed vegetables; really nice. I should mention that the scallops were cooked perfectly, not overdone like many restaurants have a tendency to do. The kids had a burger, chicken and french dip sandwiches which were all solid if nothing special. I can say the burger was cooked perfectly medium as requested. The accompanying french fries were excellent (and a great match with my Belgian style beer)! Deserts were good but nothing special. Chocolate peanut butter cake, cheesecake, etc, probably made elsewhere and shipped in but all tasty nonetheless. I was reluctant at first but pleasantly surprised by my experience at Timber Grill. The dining room is cozy and everything was fresh and well prepared and all the young servers were pleasant and attentive. I would recommend this place, especially for large groups when it's hard to please everyone.

text: Old Pueblo Grille is a place I've eaten at so frequently that amongst my clique it is known only as "OPG" for simplicity. It pains, me, therefore to plop down a mediocre two stars at a restaurant that a year ago could have easily been four. The restaurant industry is no doubt challenged, and you can see and taste the results at OPG. A recent menu shift saw some changes to what I considered to be OPG staples. The once savory and flavorful fajitas are now somewhat dry and unseasoned. The OG burger remains a favorite, but the normal bun has been replaced with an oversized "torta" bun. Why? No idea, but it is, at best, a break even change. What is not break even is the change to what must be frozen french fries...the cardboard texture is sadly prevalent. The Sonoron parm, a great addition to the menu from a ways back, has moved from three (two at lunch) chicken breasts to a single super jumbo breast. I always wonder about the freshness of chicken of this size. My strong hunch is the chicken is now frozen. Cottage cheese as a side has disappeared. The fish and chips was quite good in the past, with a lightly spicy tartar sauce as a twist. My last try found the fish slightly dry, possibly frozen, and the fries to be the stale cardboard variety described above. The corn muffins remain ho-hum, made edible by the seasoned butter. Other items, such as the pulled pork remain strong contenders. The machaca is still good and this writer likes to use the chipotle sauce adorning each table. Some changes seem positive, such as removing the jalapeno bacon, which was previously over spiced to the point of losing the subtle smokey bacon taste in a maelstrom of spice. The atmosphere remains amazing, but having recently experienced a totally empty dining room and witnessed the wait staff sent home, I wonder how long it can last. Changing the good and going frozen will never succeed...here's to hoping a new incarnation can spring up soon and save this great midtown venue.

My first day there, I did a lot of the touristy stuff near Independence Hall and ended up eating at Sonny's. It was really good, so I figured the big-name "classic" cheesesteak places must be mind-blowingly orgasmic. My last day in the city, I decided to go to Jim's for my ultimate cheesesteak experience. I was severely underwhelmed. The line was to the door. The workers were rather unfriendly. The preparation was sloppy (I hate hate hate onions and they were carelessly being flung around on the same spatula as was used for the meat. Needless to say, I had onion chunks in my sandwich.) and the seating situation was ridiculous. We had to stand around upstairs for close to 5 minutes waiting for a table to open up. Now for the sandwich: aside from the aforementioned onion chunks, the sandwich was just blah. I finished it because I was starving, not because it was delicious. I've had better cheesesteaks from pizza places in my tiny hometown in Texas. Just saying... Next time I go to Philly, I'll make a beeline for Sonny's. Jim's seems to be all hype.

text: A couple of caveats: this place is inside a weird shopping mall, next to a nondescript Mexican bakery and a Circle K. You would never know there is a Chinese restaurant there - the decor is old, not kitch and not "retro" just old. So the curb appeal is not there. It is however, spotless. BUT= do not let that deter you from going in. This is the best Chinese food ever. It is always consistent, always hot, always well prepared and always quick. Especially if you are vegetarian because they also make the best "fake" meat dishes. My partner loves their Fake Mongolian Beef, and I have a fondness for their Fake Kung Pao Chicken. My fave is the vegetarian Egg Foo Yung - amazingly good. We also order the veggie Sizzling Rice Soup and the Veggie Potstickers. The other night we also ordered (real) Orange Chicken for my brother, who loved it. The portions are huge. I have been coming here for at least 23 years, and before I stopped eating meat, at many of the meat dishes and I have never been disappointed. The Family style menu is $14-15 per person, the entrees are around $10. We usually get out of there spending around $35 for dinner with the soup, drinks and potstickers. Also, if you want to drink water, ask for a large glass - they have a tendency to serve in small juice glasses, and I have to ask for refills about 28 times before I leave.

text: I used Nature's Gallery Florist for my wedding flowers. We didn't have many flowers at our wedding because the venue was pretty intense, and we didn't want to take away from it. We got two bouquets and two boutonnieres. I originally went to another florist who made some prototypes right in front of us, but the quote for these four items was pretty insane (about $600.00). I did like the prototype, though, so I went to NGF and told Gabriella what they looked like/what we wanted. She gave us a quote, it was much more reasonable, and we were told that the flowers would be delivered to our hotel in Center City on the day of. I was a little anxious because I wasn't sure what they'd actually turn out to look like, but they were perfect - they looked almost identical to what we made with the original florist during our consultation. One negative: one piece of greenery on my husband's boutonniere fell off (it was windy on our wedding day) and as a result the whole thing flipped upside down before the ceremony started. Since we got the magnetic version instead of the pin version (Gabriella said they're easier to use) there was no way of stopping it from flipping over. It turned out not to matter, though, because those types of things never matter in the end. Final things to consider: The photo book that they have for you to look through doesn't do their flowers justice. Also, Gabriella was really accessible through email, which is good if you're like me and want to have everything in writing to refer back to later!

The Grilled Cheeserie accepts credit cards. The "make your own melt" is $5, chips $1, tomato soup $2, and specialty melts $7. The sandwich was good and crispy but I will try something more exciting next time. text: I came into Pumpkin with very high expectations and they were eagerly met. It only took us mere seconds to smell the delicious fall/winter flavors erupting from the bowls. We all mixed the ingredients thoroughly and indulged in warming soup bliss. I chose the risotto for my second dish. The creme fraiche and caramelized were perfect accompaniments to this savory and satisfying dish. I got a taste of the pork belly and it was so perfectly cooked that it didn't even require the other things on the plate with it. Course 3 was a Garrotxa cheese plate (which I had never heard of before this meal). It was sliced thinly and served with pistachio, kumquat and vanilla. The kumquat and cheese together were just a thing of beauty, both to look at and taste. For the main course, I chose the duck confit (how could I not) with lentils, purple mustard and foie gras. Yes, I smeared foie gras on confit duck and ate it. I'm sure that there is a new spot in hell for me after that move. During this course, the conversation came to a screeching halt. We all had such sensory overload from the amazing flavors that we were unable to really form sentences. Dessert, which also blew my mind was a caramelized white chocolate goat cheese cheesecake. If that alone isn't enough to sell you, perhaps the ginger and asian pear are. At this point in the meal, we all laughed at how ridiculously awesome it tasted. I'm not normally a dessert guy but this was truly something to behold. That concludes my experience for the Sunday night tasting menu. I can't wait to come back again to this wonderful, intimate and highly delicious restaurant.

text: Amazing food. Just simply amazing. Home-cooked, fresh ingredients, and very reasonable prices; as a college student, I very much appreciate a nice meal that is decently priced. The place is known for having "the best spring rolls in St. Louis"; they certainly do not disappoint. I've had the chicken, tofu, and beef spring rolls and they are all fresh and delicious! Certainly the best spring rolls I have ever had, at least. As for entrees, they offer a relatively wide selection, considering it's such a small restaurant with a small family-based staff working it. The shaking beef is absolutely marvelous! And the noodle bowls are wonderfully satisfying. Matched with a delicious Vietnamese iced coffee, you're set to go! Always ask about the specials. My father is especially a fan of "Dewey's Special Spicy Vegetarian Soup" which is made with hot spices and vegetarian beef substitute - it's a special family recipe that my father now "lives for". The service is friendly and courteous, we've had the same waiter all the times we've been to Banh Mi So #1 and he's polite and fun to talk to. He offered us his personal recommendations as well as background stories behind the food and his family. The service can be slow, but that's to be expected from such a small restaurant with an even smaller staff. You can avoid the wait altogether by simply calling ahead with your order and there is a menu on their website, banhmiso1.com. We did that today and they had our food ready by the time we arrived at the restaurant not twenty minutes later. Either way, this restaurant's food is entirely worth the wait, and if you are in St. Louis looking for great Vietnamese cuisine, do not miss your chance to come here!!

text: On October 18,2011 I purchased a 1966 Mustang convertible from Golden Classics through EBAY. Before bidding on this car, I called Golden Classics relative to the car. I informed them that I did not want to buy a car without matching numbers. I was informed that the numbers matched on this car. I ask if it was rust free and was told that it had been restored by the previous owner.. I was told that it had factory air, power steering, power brakes and a power top.. I was told that it ran well and the only thing that did not work on it was the Air. I bought the car based upon pictures, communication with a Golden Classic representative and the fact that the EBAY account through which it was advertised indicated that they had in the number of 400 sales and a 100 percent customer rating.. I didn t receive the car until December 22, 2011, That was in excess of 60 days from the date I paid them, I feel that this was intentional as EBAY requires the response from the sale be made within 60 days. When the car arrived, It was not what they said it was. In the pictures of the undercarriage, they indicate it is very clean. We found that the undercarriage was power sprayed and painted to cover a substantial amount of rust. The exterior paint has bubbles in several spots that are rust spots. None of the Gauges worked on the car including the speedometer gauge. The ball joints were shot, the speedometer drive gear was worn out. The clutch was worn out. In process of working on the transmission, the mechanic found that it is not the original transmission. It is a 68 transmission, therefore the numbers do not match. This car instead of being a show car is a bad project car. I have now spent 3,885.00 to get it in running condition. The paint job is poor and the seats have tears in them. Do not believe in all EBAY ratings as they can be manipulated by parties selling small parts to one another and then giving themselves excellent ratings to build up the account. Sometimes the parts do not even move off the shelves, it is merely a ploy to build a strong rated account. Never buy a vehicle from this company unless you personally inspect it and drive it. When a company tells you that the car has matching numbers and it doesn't, this is mere deception. This car was never worth the amount I paid for it. I paid based upon trust in a company that wasn't worthy of that trust. It is too bad that they cannot be honest. My mechanic said that this car will continue to be a project as the engine has been hammered.

text: I LOVE RDHD!! I was only introduced to this dance fitness class less than a year ago, but I am HOOKED! I took dance classes for 15 years, but there is still so much I can do to make myself feel challenged by the steps. The movements are designed so that ANYONE can do them and feel sexy, flirty, and like you're getting a great workout (which you are!) My favorite part of RHDF is the performance songs because that's when you really feel like you're starring in a musical or dancing next with Beyonce in a music video. The instructor uses one song to teach you the moves that you'll do in the performance song (which are mostly moves you do in other dances--so it's easy to catch on!), while not letting your heart rate drop. Then we go into the performance song and perform the combination of dance steps straight through a few times. Even if you've never taken a dance class before, you'll feel so confident at the end of the song when you've performed the steps several times in a row. This is what makes RHDF unique--it's the same kind of adding-on technique you might find in a step class, but it doesn't take the entire class to build the routine (which was something that always drove me batty about step--can we just move on to something different already??) Also, your heartrate doesn't drop while you're learning the moves, which makes it different from an actual dance class and ensures that you're getting a great cardio workout the whole hour. Check out www.redhotdancefitness.com and find out where you can take a class. Alison King Red Hot Dance Fitness Instructor

text: I am writing this first part of my review as I am on my way out the door to Last Word. I have armored myself to expect two things, based on the numerous reviews here: 1.A crotchety and unkind attitude from the staff. 2.A very lowball offer on the 100-odd books I am bringing in to sell (50 cents to $1.00 each) POST VISIT: I brought in two bags with around 100 books. It was a mix of hard cover and quality paperback (no regular/small paperback,) with about 10 old editions of Dorothy Parker novels. Also some sheet music books that retail new for $25+. Larry (the owner?) asked me to leave them overnight, which I did, and he called me this morning with an offer of $25 with 'about half a bag' that he wasn't going to take at all. "Most of these are so common, you know, you can get them online for ten cents..." and that even the Dorothy Parker "...sell online for $5, maybe $10, but I definitely want them." The offer was FAR MORE INSULTING than I could have ever prepared myself for. As I said, based on other reviews I was expecting an offer of 50 cents to a dollar per book that he wanted, which would have added up to at least $50. Just to give some perspective... HE isn't going to be selling these books for the alleged ten cents they sell for online. He'll likely charge 1/2 of the cover price, maybe more considering he has notoriously high prices (again, see other reviews.) If a book retails for $25, he's going to sell it for $12.50. Even offering me just 10% of the price he intends to sell it for would be $1.25. But based on his offer of $25 for the full 75 books he's taking, he's offering me 33 cents. I understand that the second hand market is rough, but there is a fine line between justifiably making a lowball offer because it may take you some time to turn around the inventory and it's an unsure investment, and just trying to rip people of because you think that you can. THIRD EDIT!!! I went back to the store to pick up my books. I figured the process would be fairly easy. My friend parked by the sidewalk and I went in. I saw my bags, with about 1/4th of my books in them. So obviously Larry had separated my books and kept them that way. The woman that was there had no idea what was going on and said he would be back in a few minutes. Since I had my friend waiting in her car I was kind of peeved, but I said I would wait. After five minutes he wasn't back, and I asked her if she could call him to see how soon his return would be. "He doesn't have his cell phone." I told her I would have to leave and come back on the 26th, but just then Larry came in. I told him I was declining his offer and was just picking up my books. He gave me this look and said "Well look, how much were you looking for? Because I could maybe give you a little bit of a better offer..." but I told him no thank you, that I would just like to take back my books. Perturbed, he told me they were in a box on the floor, and I began unloading them back into my bags. I could feel him glaring holes into the back of my head, so when I was done I lifted up my bags and said "Thank you so much for the time you spent, have a good holiday!" He replied, in the smarmiest, bitchiest voice you can possibly imagine: "Yeah well. I *did* spend a lot of time. Like, an hour and a half." To which I replied, rather pointedly: "Well. That *is* the business you are in." And then I left... never to return.

It is difficult not to be Americanized when you run restaurant business. So I give them credit for preserve their traditions. I have few advices for those who are not familiar with Korean food but willing to try. Start with 'Seafood Pancake' (Haemul Pajeon). It is very good to share as appetizer. Then go for Grilled beef ribs (Gal Bi). It comes with 5 small vege/fish dishes, very traditional. Then stuff yourself with 'Dolsot Bibim bap', rice, meat, and vege cooked in a hot stone bowl. Make sure you add chili sauce on top and stir them well. Beside the seafood pancake, this is my favorite dish. In a cold winter night, it will fills the spot. My hubby love this restaurant. He had found his comfort food. We went there last Sunday night before 6pm. The place was half full. We plan to go back again this week. I will give more update later. BTW, we ordered 3 dishes, 4 beers and it costs 45 dollar including tax. This place is small but they can handle groups. I will suggest 6 people so everyone can share. text: Put shortly, this place is amazing. The food is phenomenal, the music is good and the atmosphere is exactly what you want from New Orleans. The interior feels like an old hole-in-the-wall carved out of a warehouse with wooden pillars supporting the roof and visible wood rafters. The lighting is bright enough to see your food, but dim enough to give it that great night club vibe. It's also all nonsmoking which is a huge plus for me. One word of caution, on busy nights, i.e., most of them, they give tables to people ordering food and people just getting drinks have to either sit at the bar or stand. Given that the food is so good, it's worth getting there a bit early and eating a plate or two so that you can enjoy the show at a table. In theory, you're still supposed to order food and drinks at the bar, but I found that the staff were always walking around and asking if you wanted anything else and were super friendly. So, I didn't ever need to actually order at the bar. The music we saw there was great and the venue is small enough that it's a great show no matter where you go. Luke Winslow-King was particularly amazing with his nearly-ragtime 40s style. He even brought an old 40s-era microphone that finished off the effect. The food here though is probably the most surprising. They have everything from goat cheese lamb sliders to tuna bulgogi and it's all good. My wife and I ate here twice and had six of the few dozen dishes with our favorites being the bulgogi rice bows and the lamb sliders. The feta fries were good, but about exactly what they sounded like: good french fries with cold feta crumbled over them. The sweet potato gnocchi were delicious, but the pork roast they came with didn't do very much for me. During happy hour they also have $4 really small plates. We had the beef empanadas which were delicious, and bacon-wrapped, cheddar-stuffed figs which sounded better than they were. Really, the only downside for me was that the drinks were only so-so. The tap selection consisted of 6 mostly local and light beers and as a self-admitted beer snob, I was a little disappointed, but liked the Brooklyn Octoberfest fine. The cocktail list wasn't exactly my cup of tea either, but they made a good cucumber-mint-lime virgin drink for my pregnant wife, so they were at least accommodating.

Also, because you can bake it as long or as little as you want, you won't have to worry about getting a pie with the bottom crust being blackened from a dirty oven or from being baked too long. text: I really can not begin to explain how disappointed I am in this place. To all the Yelp reviewers who said good things- thanks for nothing. The service wasn't bad, as some Yelpers have noted, it was nonexistent. Despite four pilled-out employees staring at us we ended up seating ourselves. Eventually the waitress shambled over and mumbled some apologies about the wait. Clearly the combination of methadone and xanies was making it hard to serve all 10 customers. I then made the mistake of ordering the "Irish" breakfast. Sweet baby Jesus. Perhaps my problem is that I know what an Irish breakfast is supposed to be. This was a sad tasteless parody made all the more excruciating by the 12 dollar price tag. Here's my three-step suggestion to whoever had the gall to call the plate of crap I received an Irish breakfast- 1) go to Ireland. 2) Order an Irish breakfast at the worst, grimiest gas station you can find. 3) Feel deep shame that a Polish gas station attendant cooking with a microwave managed to make a better Irish breakfast than you. Really, its that bad. Make no mistake- it's hard to mangle a fry-up like these folks do. The tiny, tiny piece of what I will generously describe as white pudding had been dumped into a frier and reduced into a wizened little nugget. The "bangers" were much more like crappy american breakfast sausages (think Jimmy Dean) than true Irish bangers and had similarly been deep fried into oblivion. There was NO BLACK PUDDING! Shame, shame. The rashers were weirdly tasteless. Making wildly salty Irish bacon bland is a negative achievement for the Epic Fail Halls of Shame. Luckily the inattentive waitress did manage to perk up for the billing part of the transaction, happily appearing with our $29 bill and putting an end to our nightmare. In the few months I've lived in Philly I've had plenty of excellent meals so I suppose I was eventually bound to get the whammy. But for my betrayer to be my favorite childhood meal is cruel indeed. If you're craving a fry-up in Philadelphia, try the Dark Horse Pub on 2nd St.

text: Overpriced considering the amount and quality of food you get for that price. We ordered a vegetarian platter as one of the starters, among others, because there were six of us there, so we figured we'd be able to try the different items on the plate. The plate arrived with one samosa cut into two, one aloo tikki cut into two and two pakoras, for $9, totally not worth it! We ordered chicken malabar ($8), a tiny breast of flattened chicken, battered with coconut and deep fried, enough for one person. For main course: mixed non-veg tandoori grille ($23), which looked and sizzled like it would be the best tasting dish on earth, but after tasting it, it was quite bland, enough to the point that my husband had to send it back to have some moreflavor added. They brought it back with some tikka masala sauce thrown over it, which now made it a curry instead of the tandoori grilled dish! I ordered Chicken Tikka Masala, which i must say was tasty, but, in the entire karai (serving bowl), there were barely 5-6 tiny little pieces of chicken and the rest of it was the curry which was gravy. At $14, again this item is not worth it. We also ordered Lamb Rogan Josh ($17) which was ok, Daal Makhani and Mutter Paneer ($12 which is high for small portions of veg dishes) tasted good. We also ordered a side of Raita. It came in a little saucer like container, which again was only enough for one person ($3). Since this place is BYO, we brought our own wine, which they did not help serve. But they charged a $5 corkage fee for opening and pouring it ourselves! Although the servers are polite, service is ok. They constantly forget to bring things and mistakes. Complimentary chutney & papadam these days is not a big deal. Most indian restaurants do that obligingly. We got one plate of a couple pieces of papadum, but since there were six of us, it was not enough for all of us, so we asked for more. We never got it. We used our Restaurant.com $25 voucher, but I think i would rather take me and my foodie guests somewhere else worth our while, our dollars and our palates.

text: This place was surprisingly good and a lot of fun. I was in Boise with family recently and we wanted to get some food. Since we were in the mood for Japanese food, we decided to check out Shige. I was visiting from Boston, so I wanted to see what local scene had to offer. One thing about Boise since I was there last was how much development has been going on. I spent a lot of time in Boise as a kid and it's not until you're much older you really start seeing the change and really start appreciating everything. Because of the local college, there is definitely a much younger demographic and a lot more interesting restaurants cropping up. Shige was just another one of the places, but its definitely one place that you have to try out if happen to find yourself in downtown Boise. Tucked away in a food complex of sorts, it takes some effort to find, or you'll miss it. Right on the strip that is N Main, this is one that should be at the top of your list. Very much like the style of Benihana, where the food is cooked right in front of you, Shige offers a bit more classier version of dining. With chairs all around the grill, this is the ideal place for a group to have some fun, watch the chef work his magic and have some delicious food. There is plenty of food to be had so be prepared to feast. Each meal comes with your choice of meat, veggies and/or seafood. Everything is cooked in sections, therefore you will be getting your veggies cooked, then your meat and finally your rice. The staff is very helpful and friendly, especially the chefs themselves. They were very pleasant, funny and were clearly enjoying their job. It created a great vibe and a fun dining experience. Surprisingly, Shige offered some really good sushi as well. Elaborate and somewhat intimidating, there are plenty of options to choose from. If you are in the crispy or soft mood, there is something for everyone. Shige is a great place to dine and have some solid Japanese food in the Boise area. If I find myself back in town, I will definitely be going again. Not only do you get some good food, you will have plenty of fun. I am glad I had to chance to experience this place.

text: So glad that Kristian's has returned as Kris. The food is stellar. Our group had dinner on a Saturday night. Our appetizers included the charred radicchio, which was perfectly balanced, the grilled octopus, the braised calamari and the mussels. Both octopus dishes were outstanding. I don't know how I would choose among them the next time. The grilled octopus was very light with a perfect texture. The braised calamari comes in an incredible tomato broth. Another in our group had the mussels with Italian sausage and said they were among the best he's ever had. He wanted to order a second mussels for his entree. The mussel broth was divine. The gnocchi pasta is the lightest gnocchi I have ever tasted. It may be the best pasta dish on the menu. The tube pasta in the octopus puttanesca sauce was also outstanding. Several in our group ordered the trout and loved it. The accompanying parsnip puree and brussel sprout slaw made the dish. The ricotta donuts were the hands down favorite dessert. Unique and special. Go hungry and bring friends. The portions, including many of the "small" plates, are substantial.

text: My wife and I went to Otto's last night for dinner, and it was excellent German food. I would have given it five stars if the atmosphere was just a little bit more updated, and our dessert wasn't on the stale side. I think these are the only things holding this restaurant back. We just moved to this area in June and I've been passing this place by all the time and always wondered what the food and beer selection was like. It was great! Now it's not gourmet food by any means, but it's great food for cold winter nights. We met up with some of my in-laws at the bar, the tap selection was impressive and they had a little bit of everything, it's kind of hard not to have a good beer with 23 taps. The bartender was friendly and helpful with letting me try out a beer I had never heard of before. We took our drinks to our table and looked over our menus. Our group decided to go only German and not get any of the non-German offerings. We ordered the Rauchfleisch and Potato Pancakes for our appetizers. The Rauchfleisch was more or less us just being adventurous and trying something new. It was good but probably something none of us would order again. The Potato Pancakes on the other hand were great and definitely something we'll order again. My wife and mother-in-law tried the Snapper Soup, and both were raving about it. My Chicken Orzo soup was definitely homemade and tasted good. Our entrees that we ordered were the Jaeger Schnitzel, Schweinepfeffer, Neuschwanstein and the Sausage Sampler. The only complaint with entrees was with my brother-in-laws order, the Jaeger Schnitzel. It wasn't because of the taste but rather the portion size. He seemed quite happy with it after tasting it though and plowed through it. My Sausage Sampler was fantatstic and anybody who loves German Sausages should be all over this one. I had this with their amazing sauerkraut and spaetzle with gravy. The Bratwurst was my favorite with the Hungarian Brat following a close second. Our finale was the German Chocolate Cake, and it was a let down. After all that great German food the cake ended up being stale with not enough of the caramel coconut that was the best part of it. Overall though the food was great and we'll be heading back there again. We're looking forward to trying the outside seating when the weather gets warmer out. For the beer people out there I found two great beers here. The Bavarian Barbarian (which is not listed on the menu and may be a seasonal) and the Hofbrau Dunkel. Two dark beers with great flavor.

We all split an appetizer tray with bacon chicken wings (SO good), spicy peas, steak bites and some kind of cheese toast. I went for the top sirloin as a main, with wasabi infused mashed potatoes and vegetables. The potatoes were good, but I didn't really taste the whole wasabi thing. Good mashed potatoes, but nothing special. The steak....ohhhh the steak was unbelievable. Cooked to the perfect medium rare, tender, juicy...oh I'm getting hungry again. Their dessert menu is seriously tempting, and I got the sampler which had a slice of chocolate cake (meh..it was chocolate cake), a mini raspberry crème brulée (pretty tasty) and the pièce de résistance...a small slice of their carribean rum cake. If nothing else, PLEASE go to Chop to get this cake. It is the best rum cake I've ever had. It was rum-y and cinnamon-y and coconut-y and everything good in the world-y. Service was excellent. The waitress was friendly, chatty when appropriate, good at recommendations, helpful and very prompt and attentive. The prices are fairly cha-ching but I left seriously satisfied (and I wasn't paying anyways, so who cares). The restaurant got very, very busy so I would suggest reservations if you're planning on trying it out. And you really should. Go now. Seriously.

text: First, the good: the server was incredibly friendly and helpful. The niceties end there, sadly. I'm going to go dish by dish to make sure I don't miss any of the misery. Potato Wedges (Tz'iips) These were fine, albeit unsalted; however it's hard to mess fried potatoes up. Kefta Dry, flavorless rice with tiny little vegan meatballs. The meatballs had a decent flavor but there were only three of them. I paid $7.50 for three tiny turd-looking things and some dry basmati. Disappointing, but not so much that we didn't give them a second chance. Mujadera This was the reason we came. A layered dish of rice, spicy lentils, and caramelized onions? I could practically taste the rich, oily goodness. What did we get? Possibly the saddest dish I've had all year. The rice was dry like in the kefta, the lentils were dry and crumbly with almost no flavor, and the onions were NOT caramelized and barely even onions: they were dehydrated shallots. Crunchy and dry like bits of parchment. I literally had to put the ketchup from my potatoes on the onions to choke them down. Upon first glance my dining partner thought they were some bizarre wood chip garnish. How can a chef get away with that? Just so we're on the same page, caramelized onions are sliced onions slow-cooked over low heat with lots of nommy fat. The end result is something soft, rich and luxurious. This was paper. I cannot believe the menu lies in this way. Garlic Hummus and Bessara with Pita The pita tasted like it had been frozen and heated up in a microwave. incredibly tough and unpleasant. The hummus was unsalted. I'm barely a cook but I have no idea how one can make hummus without salt. The bessara just tasted like spicy cumin. Sign me up for Sabra any day over what Meze offers. Shawarma This was just an embarrassment to vegans and vegetarians. Totally flavorless. I was forced to employ my ketchup once again to make it palatable. It was the same tough-as-rubber pita stuffed with shredded cabbage and some tomatoes in what tasted like diluted vegenaise. The veggie chicken inside was fine (we confirmed it was not made on site: what a surprise!) but tasted better dipped in ketchup like a child's chicken mcnugget than in the pathetic vegenaise sauce. I don't know what is up with this place; is there just nothing else veg-friendly in st. petersburg? This was some of the worst food I've ever eaten. I'm really disappointed in the sandwich as everyone on yelp has good reviews, not to mention the fact that I'm still hungry. Perhaps I should try dine-in and see how that turns out. My wife had the bun tom nuong (noodle dish with shrimp and fish sauce), which was also very good. Fish sauce was excellent. Prices were a little higher than normal for Vietnamese restaurants, but for an extra couple bucks for the pho, you get a much nicer atmosphere and friendlier service than at Kien Giang. text: I visited the Quincy Street Bistro on 6/4 as part of a group of 3 people. We had gotten reviews from a friend who knows one of the owners and was familiar with all the work they had done to fix up the building. They have parking across the street, which is convenient but not the easiest to cross the street. We got there and the place was pretty full and loud. The bar looks pretty nice, but the street-level floor has very little on the walls and no carpet, making for the noise level to be so high that the three of us had a hard time even talking to each other. We sat in a small back room and it was even louder back there, probably because there were a few tables with large, loud groups, but the building and room decor (or lack thereof) just didn't help it. I was suprised at how large their menu is. However, for a "bistro", and for something described as a "Gastropub" or casual "new American", the menu seemed more like south St. Louis run of the mill bar and grill. Although there were many options on the menu, nothing screams culinary creativity or unique "American" food For starters, we had an order of the Tavern Chips with horseradish sauce. The sauce was pretty good, but the chips were cut too thick and were soggy, oily and tasted like wet cardboard dipped in oil. If you didn't smear them on the sauce, they were barely edible. For food, we ordered a few different sandwiches. We skipped the meatloaf, although I was thinking it would be a twist on the classic, the description was too honest to really make it attractive (seasoned ground beef baked with ketchup). My friend started with the Quincy Street Monster dog - a half pound hot dog served deep fried. He said it was good, but that it tasted exactly like you'd expect a generic deep fried giant hotdog to taste. Other than size, there was nothing special about this "Monster Dog". My other friend ordered the chicken fried steak and was thoroughly disappointed. It was too dry, bland... and looked like something out of a TV dinner box. I had a cajun burger, cooked "medium". It was described on the menu as "dredged" in blackening spices, but in reality this was a decent sized tasteless hunk of hamburger. I really could not taste the spices, and the Pepper Jack cheese did not help the sandwich. The burger was served with fries (although cottage cheese was an option too), and the fries were decent - salty, skinny fries - somewhat reminiscent of steak n' shake fries. Their iced tea did not taste freshly brewed - I think it may have been a mix. Overall, I was disappointed and will not be back. There were a few positives about the meal - the servers were very nice and attentive, the portions were very generous, and we didn't have to wait too long for our food. I really hope this place makes it - it is good to have these sort of businesses in the neighborhood and the owners obviously put a lot into rehabbing the building, but the location will not make up for the mediocrity of the bar-grill food.

text: After an especially hot and steamy viewing of Showgirls and a quick flip through the spring Victoria's Secret catalogue, I was in the mood for more cheap thrills. My pulse racing like I just got out of spin class, I arrived at Hooters on a Saturday like so many others, ready to take in the view, devour some delicious wings, and try not to embarrass myself while being chatted up by a college girl in a white and orange Halloween costume. To my delight, it was Wrestling Day, and all of the waitresses were dressed as professional wrestlers. Appropriate, as my hung over waitress would have been better cast as The Undertaker. As I would soon find out, the "viewing" beats the chewing. I ordered the all-you-can-eat boneless wings. As my dedicated readers know, I have a debilitating fear of birds, and believe touching their bones allows the bird's soul to torment me in the afterlife, so I generally stick to boneless wings. There I was, lounging sideways in my booth with my legs crossed, taking my first bite of a buffalo wing through my Mexican wrestler facemask with a manic look in my eyes, content with all in the world and expecting nothing but the best from the chefs at Hooters. What the sauce lacked for in quality it made up for in butter. However, the meat itself was like a dry piece of roadkill cartilage sprayed with the foam they use to seal cracks in your basement walls. And I know, having eaten my share of roadkill in my many trips to Nigeria to complete business deals with dying diamond mine heiresses. I asked for more wings after dumping the remaining 9 1/2 wings on my plate on the floor under my table, and elected to go with the teriyaki wings. While chatting me up during a particularly long refill of my diet Dr. Pepper, my waitress asked me about my cell phone cover and asked if she could show the other waitresses. I didn't understand all the fuss about my custom self-portrait on the phone cover, but I figured it was harmless to let them admire it. Upon checking my phone later in the day, I noticed someone called Puerto Rico 11 times! After a few minutes, my teriyaki wings came out. They had a corporate tang, a hint of mild depression - a charity-dinner appetizer made for 200 people in a sleezy Bangkok convention center. Needless to say, I dumped those as well, this time using my foot to discreetly push the growing graveyard of wasted chicken lives further under the table while coughing and waving at the hostess standing by the door to cover my movements. I decided to take my final order to go, and because they apparently don't allow that on the all-you-can-eat option, I was forced to stick all 5 parmesan garlic wings in the pocket of my slacks. I give 1 star for the wrestling promotion and the lovely Mexican wrestling mask (I plan to wear it often at home), and 1 additional star because I caught a 4 pound large-mouthed bass the next day when I used the parmesan garlic wings as bait. Delightfully "Tackley", Yet Unrefined indeed! I'll be sending them the dry-cleaning bill for my slacks. Be warned, vampire pick-pockets - the stench of garlic in my pockets is strong enough to kill.

text: The Brick House is average, no more and no less. The property is an old converted bank. A pretty cool space that is dumbed down by the hideous overuse of fake antiques and liquor/beer banners. I'm not sure why any non-chain would decorate the restaurant to be a poor copy of a TGI Fridays, but that's what you get here. The bar area is spacious with lots of tables and bar seating. The one thing I don't get is that there are several TV's above the bar, not all showing sports. Fine, ok for those that want to watch sports (you would assume). Yet one of the TV's is always on the Food Network. While I really like the Food Network, I have to laugh at the irony of watching soME of the world's greatest chefs cook in a restaurant that strives to be average. Let's go to service. It's solid, especially at the bar. I will admit I do go here often for the bar. It gets a decent crowd on the usual nights and the staff does make it enjoyable. As for the food, I'll actually start with the menu. Classic mistakes here. The menu is way too big. Another reason the food can only achieve average taste levels. But that's not the worst part. The actual menu is a visual nightmare. Think of it a throwing up words, visuals and colors on page after page. My friends and I laugh every time we see it. As designers, this is clearly a case where the restaurant wanted to save a buck. Instead, it makes it very hard to read, and leads to less than stellar opinions about the food itself. Most of the menu items have a very familiar taste. I've eaten here many times because I know what I'm getting. Average, barely seasoned and probably not that fresh, but after a drink or two, it's not really the point anyway. While I would not classify this as a "frozen/canned" kitchen, it's not far from going in that direction. My advice to the owner: Drop the menu to 30 or fewer items. 100+, it is impossible for the kitchen to excel. Start buying obviously fresh ingredients. Remove the tacky decor and video games. Let the property speak for itself. And get rid of the lame DJ on weekend nights. It's awful and distracting. The three drunk girls and really lame guy that take to the floor strikes me as a bad vegas show. Finally, allow more input from your staff. They're actually pretty good and can tell you what works. So average across the board but a little up-tick for the staff. IF YOU FOUND THIS REVIEW HELPFUL, PLEASE RATE IT AND SEND A COMMENT.

text: I know that Sunday's tend to be the "b" team working and that wait staff are generally less enthusiastic due to large parties, screaming kids, and the ever unpopular "church crowd" that tends to act more like unruly, disrespectful heathen, not to mention the smaller than average tips that seem to circulate on Sunday's. That being said...went to Old Chicago on Sunday and had a really unpleasant experience. We were seated at 12:40. There were not many people in the restaurant. Maybe 3/10 tables had people at them, and I think that is being generous. We were the only larger party when we arrived. One other party of 8ish arrived about 30 minutes after we did. But the tables really were not filling up and it stayed about 20-30% capacity while we were there. Our food arrived at the table at 2:08. Yes, that is almost an hour and a half with just our water/soda's on the table. Our waitress never came to apologize for the wait or to let us know how much longer the wait would be. And when our food finally did arrive, our server hadn't even noticed that one of the entree's was completely missing from the order. And there were also 2 entree's that were wrong. I will grant you, we were a larger party. There were 8 of us. But that means that 3/8 orders were messed up in some way. Not a very good stat. 62.5% accuracy. At this point, we asked to speak to a manager. It actually took 2 requests to get the manager out. I get that he may have been busy...but making an angry customer wait is just not a great idea. Once the missing order/wrong orders were made known, he should have immediately come to the table to apologize for that... But I am getting a little ahead of myself. The reason I am writing this review is not just because we had to wait a long time or that our food was wrong. Well, technically, yes those are the reasons...but more than that, it was because there was SO much that could have been done PROACTIVELY to keep this from becoming such a bad experience. 1- If it is going to be a long wait (if 30 min has elapsed and food is not in the window ready to go out) the server needs to be communicating with the table. Let us know that you are on top of it!! Let us know that you are aware that we have been waiting. Let us know how much longer we should expect to wait. Let us know that it MATTERS to you; because honey, your tip depends on our experience. 2- If you have a table that has been waiting more than an hour for food, something needs to be done. First, let your manager know and see what can be done to expedite things. Second, consider doing something like a free appetizer. I am not saying give away the kitchen, but even garlic bread would have been SOMETHING to keep the growling stomachs at bay. And who knows, we may have liked it enough to order it as an appetizer in the future. As it stands, it is pretty questionable whether any of us will be going back to an Old Chicago. Ever. 3- As I mentioned above, If orders are missing/wrong after that long of a wait (especially when you are not terribly busy) get your manager out there immediately. Then you are being proactive and can communicate that you are aware of the situation, and let us know what you are doing to remedy it. And mangers, if your presence has been requested...don't make us get up and go looking for you... If you are busy and cannot get away for a min, send our server back to say that it will be a couple of minutes. COMMUNICATE PEOPLE! And if I am not mistaken, managers should be out walking the floors on occasion to make sure that everything is running smoothly. I believe that is what "floor managers" or "front of house managers" are for. Each one of the above bullets has 2-4 points where things could have been done better. And they should have been done better. This was a very disappointing experience. Incidentally, mine was the order that never got placed. And when they did get around to making it and bringing it out, it was pretty unremarkable. Bummer. I will probably give them a try again....eventually... Not on a Sunday, and with only a couple people next time. See if it gets any better. I sure hope it does.

It would be ready in minutes, he told me. It wasn't. A person who had ordered a pizza 15 minutes after I did had gotten hers. When I asked again I was told it still wasn't ready. It was getting "well done." Turns out, they never put my order in. It had been cooking for only ten minutes when I went up the second time. I can understand a place gets busy, but I don't like being lied to. When I told him it was "well done enough and take it out," he said it still wasn't ready. I just got my money back (he shorted me 52 cents, too, but I was too pissed off to care or make a stink) and left. "Sorry" was all I got. Manager-owner needs to talk to its staff about customer service.

text: If NOLA native Betty N (bettygeek.yelp.com) recommends a visit to the famous ACME Oyster House, then you definitely must make it a point to do so. As part of the NOLA in 12 hours adventure, ACME was supposed to be the first stop but a "45 minute" dinner wait dissuaded Mathew M and me, ultimately landing us at MiLa (which I highly recommend). The following day I made it priority because I wanted to try their amazing Étouffée...and of course, their raw oysters. I arrived 15 minutes prior to opening (they open at 11am) and as you would conclude, a line was already formed. An employee came out to take names and party size but I was ensured to be seated with thee first wave of patrons. As 11am rolled around, doors opened and patrons were given personal seating preference. I opted to dine at the bar where I had a front row seat to all the shucking action. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_ab50qdWOk0DdB6XOrBitw?select=HaT1psV6l8TU__PXu-wFHw What's so impressive was after they took my order, I quickly visited the restroom to wash my hands and by the time I returned my entire order was waiting for me! Oh, and by the way, their staff is very attentive and friendly. Raw Oysters ($8.75 for 1/2 dz or $13.50 for a dz): 5/5 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_ab50qdWOk0DdB6XOrBitw?select=MnqJ4vIqZu_3QqBg6vwL6g http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_ab50qdWOk0DdB6XOrBitw?select=HUtc9ME0RmjLPLGlX8DrSA Okay, I'm not much of an oyster fan...and I'll confess I didn't care much for Kumamoto oysters at Providence on Melrose in Los Angeles (http://www.yelp.com/biz/providence-los-angeles-2) but these were some truly remarkable oysters! I was served some humongous, soft, sweet oysters that has turned me into a believer. My only regret was ordering a half dozen. I didn't go with ACME's Chargrilled based upon Betty N's recommendation and I'm glad I didn't. Seafood Étouffée ($8.99 for small or $12.99 for large): 5/5 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_ab50qdWOk0DdB6XOrBitw?select=3Ql3TNOGz8KYlWaxQTzgmA Yes, this was thee best étouffée in my life and I'm glad I had a large order! ACME's perfectly seasoned roux was so silky and blanketed soft fluffy white rice. The entire dish wasn't piping hot, making it super easy to inhale. If I could have this everyday...I would! I was out the door by 11:20am. A whopping 20 minutes spent in oyster/étouffée heaven. I'll be back for more the next time I'm in NOLA...hopefully for longer than a day. ;)

text: I'm just not a fan of this place. It really focuses on the coffee, and I'm a tea person, not a coffee person. I'd appreciate more effort on tea too. It doesn't take much effort to stock a handful of high-quality loose-leaf teas along with coffee (tea is easier to prepare well than coffee, IMHO), but this place doesn't even seem to try, it just wants to be all about its coffee. Is the coffee here good? Ehh. I do drink coffee, and I have opinions on it, although I'm certainly no expert. I will say, the stuff I've had here is good, but it is not the best coffee I've had. In order to justify its coffee-snobbery, I think this place would have needed to really like, AMAZE me with their coffee, and they failed to do this. I do like that La Colombe does direct trade -- that's great. I'm also a big fan of shade-grown coffee, both for the taste and because I like the ecological principles behind it, but currently, I have yet to sample or even see for sale a single shade-grown coffee from this company. Supposedly they have one in their "workshop", but I have yet to try it. This company is lagging behind others, there are so many good shade grown coffees on the market. What about the ambiance in this particular shop? I don't like it. The walls are red, and it feels...for lack of a better descriptor, arid, conjuring up images of parts of the American Southwest or drier parts of the Mediterranean. It doesn't feel cozy or comforting to me. There's also a sort of weird vibe here that I don't like. One of my friends articulated it to me, that there's a long line of people who seem to know a lot about coffee and know exactly what they want. The people working the counter are nice, but when I've been in here, it's been busy and high-pressure, you get to the front of the line and you don't have time for chit-chat. I don't like that sort of vibe. I'd rather go to a sort of friendly, down-to-earth cafe that offers a few shade-grown coffees and has a good tea selection too, a place where I can chat with the people behind the counter a bit without feeling like I'm imposing on the people behind me. text: Nice atmosphere, friendly and efficient service. That's where the fun ends. The food here is really sub-par considering your other options both nearby and citywide. We've eaten here twice, had different things each time, and been disappointed both times. Not angry, or disgusted, but just sort of meh. On both attempts, we found the chorizo tasted very much like bland ground beef. All portions are very small considering the prices and what you get for less elsewhere. Three merely OK fish tacos cost nearly $14, when you can get two outstanding fish tacos around the corner for less than $8. The $14 Burrito Azteca sounded exciting but disappointed, both in flavor and size--it arrived perpendicular on an oval plate, if that gives you an idea. The pork was nice, but there was little salsa verde flavor at all. And then there are the drink prices--$7 for Svedka vodka and soda. Not a large one. Not a double. You're better off ordering the house margaritas by the pitcher if you're looking for cheap drinks. I just feel like La Marg hasn't kept up since back in the day. Indy has been blessed with a huge influx of Mexican immigrants who have started serving authentic, interesting Mexican food and they're doing it for far less money and doing it better. La Marg seems like a relic of the past; when your other choices might have been Chi Chi's or Don Pablo's, you could get away with mediocrity. Maybe they're reliving their old El Mat's days, where they slid by on location alone, but I think if they hope to stick it out in up-and-coming Fountain Square, they'd better step up their game. Folks expect more than beer, chips and salsa, and a sunny patio these days.

text: Federal Donuts, where the donuts and chicken are hot and the staff is hotter. All of the forces of chaos combined, have kept me from trying out the best new eatery in Philly but recently, they became confused on the way to my house and I was able to slip through, like just about any Running Back through the Eagles soft defense. I had heard the horror stories, of how the clamoring masses have stacked body upon body, in their attempts at getting themselves a shiny donut or chicken part. I'm not good in crowds so I tried to time my arrival accordingly(around 10:30am). SUBURBAN COMMUTER NOTE: I parked on the far side of Washington, thinking there would be no space available, but upon my trek over, noticed ample spots, just a block away. Upon my arrival, there was already a small group present. Those last vestiges of the morning rush combined with the early chicken go getters and I , in my arrogance, considered myself an equal member of both camps. I immediately took in the familiar and inviting faces of Blake and Felicia. They were busy but I couldn't help but think that they considered this their " down time". Here's the part of every one of my reviews, where I make an ass of myself. I was invited to take a seat at the counter. When I got there, there was counter space but no seat. I stood (happily) and watched the goings on. After a few minutes, Felicia came out to gently explain to me that the stools pull out and she" pulled out my stool " (sorry). You'd think someone who grew up with transformers would have figured it out, but ill blame the fact that I had been up since 4am. Once properly seated, I was able to enjoy the best coffee and donuts the city (world) has to offer. I advise anyone to skip their usual cream and sugar and experience the flavor of that coffee raw. really good stuff. Granted, I was a little late to get the donuts fresh from the fryer, but damn, were they still the best I'd had and as a baker, Ive eaten cake donuts right out of the fryer before. I may have missed the hot donuts but my arrival meant I was one of the first to get a golden ticket for chicken. I was also lucky enough to have an eating companion there, who offered a mix and match scenario with the chicken so I was able to try both the Chili Garlic and the other (whose name I forget but it was the dry rub one). Both rocked my world and were just as good leftover later that night. In my time at FD, I witnessed a staff that was amazing. Blake was a fountain of donutcoffeechicken information, Felicia was the perfect "face" of the Front of the house and the BOH staff were a grim lesson in startling efficiency and ingenuity. The magic that they work in that small space was impressive. Unfortunately, there was a computer malfunction, that threatened to bring down the store's mojo. Skynet is truly taking over. Yet I watched these heroes, power through the hurdle like pros as the patient masses accepted the situation with quiet reverence, knowing that they have a good thing going here and to complain would kill it. I will cop to being a personal friend to a few of the staff here, but that should take nothing away from my great experience. There's a simplicity to Federal Donuts that will keep this endeavor afloat for as long as it wants to be. I propose to all national sports coverage, that henceforth, you can quit the cloying shots of louts making cheesesteaks in your cutaway shots and get a camera in FD, to show the real working class spirit of Philadelphia and foods that are actually appetizing. If only they could fit a camera in there....

text: OK.. as you can see from my review almost one year ago to the date, I've been to TRAX and loved it in the past. My husband ordered the special salad of the evening.. a hot salad.. it was fresh spinach, pancetta and a hot balsamic dressing. What he received was a heaping pile of cooked spinach - wilted spinach, burnt pancetta .. or was it bacon? and a dressing that looked more like a glaze.. Moving on to the entrees.. my husband ordered his usual, filet mignon, medium rare... keep in mind, between he and myself (I order it medium rare when I get it there too) we've had this entree about 8 times. I ordered the salmon with a cherry bbq demi-glace. The waiter said that the chef recommends getting the salmon at medium rare, ok, that is what I ordered. We proceeded to wait at least 40 minutes for our entrees.. after looking around and seeing everyone in the restaurant receive the entrees before us .. with the exception of the couple that sat down about 5 mins ago.. we were looking for our waiter.. anybody to notice! After looking at my watch several times and wondering where the wait staff was, our waiter finally came by .. to take the just seated couple's order.. he said "your order will be out shortly".. we waited, waited, and waited some more. In the past, this was one thing that we loved about TRAX. The wait staff was very attentive and you never had to wait for a refill of water, in fact, the waiter would fill your wine glass in this BYOB. NOPE! Not anymore! I noticed our waiter (who has been our server numerous times and commented that he recognized us) was in the back in the kitchen watching our order.. Here's what we think happened.. they totally botched our order and after noticing it, decided to get it out to us ASAP! My husband's filet was burnt on the outside as if they threw it on the grill at high temp to sear it and hope it got cooked fast enough.. And was RAW on the inside - it wasn't even warm.. The salmon was the same way! The demi-glaze was more like a gummy mess and the fish was crunchy and cooked on the outside but the middle was RAW! It was mush - it was not medium rare, it was more like sushi! Needless to say, we didn't eat it.. and again .. waited, waited, waited for the waiter to come back. he wanted to know if we needed anything and I asked him to wrap up both our entrees and that we would take them home to heat them in the oven so they weren't raw and we could eat them. OK.. here is where we get really pissed! Instead of doing some customer service to REPEAT CUSTOMERS! he began to argue with us about how the chef prepares 'medium rare' and next time we should order medium well.. OMG! I said to him.. we are repeat customers who ALWAYS get the filet and NEVER had it been rare when ordered medium rare.. Whatever! He took our plates and disappeared in the kitchen.. Do you think they inspected our plates to see if the items were RAW? NOPE! They wrapped them up and said next time, he hopes things go better. NEXT TIME??? Are you FXXing kidding me? This place is not cheap! There are tons of restaurants in the area that know how to cook steak and salmon. In fairness, he offered to comp us dessert.. nope, we were ready to get out of there! We were there for 2 hours and waited for raw food. The took nothing off the bill so we paid the $90 bucks.. left him a $7 tip and wrote we would not be back. If you want to waste you precious time and get served raw food, I highly recommend this place. If you would rather be treated professionally and served proper food.. try something else. I hear From the Boot rocks.. We'll go there next time. Oh - and just to add.. the party of 6 apparently had a disconnect on the chef's definition of medium rare or rare as they sent their plate back too and got a schooling from the waiter on how to properly order.

The salad was decent, although a bit garlicky (trust me, I eat garlic like it is going out of style, so for me to say this... it was garlicky). Now for the last and final disappointment of our experience at Cactus Creek. My husband and I both ordered the Ribeyes. I chose a side of mashed potatoes and he chose a side of mushrooms. The steaks... Why bother asking guests temperatures when the steaks are so thin, you either get slightly pink or grey (my husband ordered rare and I medium rare)? The ribeyes were literally no more than a half inch thick and about 1/3 of the steaks were composed of fat and gristle. I understand that ribeyes are a fattier cut, but nice steakhouses trim their meat, and let the beautiful marbling a ribeye has enhance the flavor. I guess I can see why they didn't trim the steaks, if they did our steaks would have resembled a petite sirloin you buy from Save Mart for $2.99 lb. It was such a huge disappointment. Not to mention, the steaks were severely lacking in flavor. My mashed potatoes were very average, nothing more nothing less. My husband's side of mushrooms seemed like they came from a can and were topped with a demi glaze from a jar. The "Sorry Charlie" sign you see while driving on the freeway, should be burned. Our bill was around $90.00 (no drinks) and my husband and I both left feeling like we had a $30.00 meal a chauncy casino. A few years back, when I was in college we ate the $7.77 Ribeye deal at the Gold Dust West, and I can honestly say I enjoyed that meal more. I wish so badly my husband and I had gone to Charlie Palmer, I would have happily paid a little bit more and spared myself the huge disappointment of shelling out $90.00 for quite possibly, the worst "steakhouse" meal I have ever had.

So that's what they did, charged me close to $16.00 per night for "resort amenities". Because we stayed for two nights and I had to pay my brother-in-law's fee, that was a whopping $60.00 for something which I still do not have an explanation for. When asked, the manager was very vague as to what the charges were about. I usually don't write negative reviews like this but Best Western Sea Wake Beach Resort was definitely the low point of my vacation. Personally, I think they get themselves off on the fact that they are so close to the beach and offer such low prices when they do have hidden costs. text: Over the last few years, Circles has come a long way. They've gone from quick-n-dirty (in a good way) takeout place to full-on dine in experience, and I have to say, I like it. Don't let the neighborhood fool you, Circles isn't located along a business district, restaurant row or hotspot central. They're the little engine that could, that neighborhood secret that's whispered from transplant to transplant like that hot local band. That is, if it's possible for a band to taste like spicy curry. But I digress, Circles is like a secret wrapped in a surprise inside a foodgasm. I've gone there for brunch, dinner and takeout late at night. I've never been disappointed. One thing I've always noticed, is the food there tastes fresh and "clean." By clean, I mean that in a lot of restaurants the food tastes like the oil it was cooked in. Here, everything seems made to order, like in much more upscale places, but at very decent prices. It seems to bridge that gap between cheap, "fast" asian food and the pricy exotic kind. Their dumplings are perfectly chewy, the pad thai & the drunken noodle dishes sometimes tend to go light on actual noodles and heavy on the veggies, and other times you get the opposite, but that little inconsistency isn't really a problem because they're A+ on flavor. I can't comment on the vegetarian dishes, but they seem to have an alternative dish for almost everything available. Every time we've eaten in, service has been excellent. Occasionally the chef will make a visit to your table to ask about the food, and it's great to see people who care enough about their product to ask. If you aren't that adventurous, they have a selection of no-so-thai food that's fairly americanized without compromising creativity or flavor, such as thai-bbq wings, cheesesteak spring rolls and a variety of soups and rice dishes that can be altered according to taste. They're all perfect after a few drinks, if you know what I mean. Personally, I'm a hot food wimp and prefer the "medium" flavor range. Let me say they nailed it, and I got exactly what I was expecting.. At only a 10 minute walk from the Passyunk corridor, if you're in the area and have a hankering for something other than pizza, cheesesteaks and overall south philly culinary nastiness, you owe it to yourself to try this place.
